title: Серьги от Ильи и обещание Макса  (Earrings from Ilya and Max's Promise)

segments.t: Realizing Ilya bought the earrings that Sasha loves so much, Max corners his rival in the hallway and demands to know what he is playing at. Unwilling to disappoint Sasha after she brags about her wonderful boyfriend, Max tells Ilya he will pay him the full price tomorrow.
Я не понял, зачем тебе это надо?
Я скажу Саше, чтобы она тебе их вернула.
Let's walk back through the scene line by line.
Я не понял, зачем тебе это надо?
'I do not understand, why do you need this?' Max questions calmly right away, weaving "ponyal" ("understood") together with "zachem" ("what for") just the way native speakers do.

'I just knew for a long time what she wanted.' Max brings a thoughtful angle at this moment, pairing "prosto" ("just") with "davno" ("for a long time") to get the point across in plain spoken Russian.
'Since she chose you instead of me.' Max chooses a calm bearing beside Sasha, building the phrase around "kak" ("how") and "vybrala" ("chose") for a crisp, natural delivery.
'Hold on a second.' Sasha shares a direct direction at this moment, anchoring the Russian line on "pogodi" ("wait") and "nu-ka" ("go on, come on") without extra filler.
'I do not know.' Max displays an emphatic mood in their talk, putting "znayu" ("know") alongside "ya" ("I") in a tight, everyday turn of phrase.
'What you are scheming.' Sasha sustains a sharp direction right away, joining "zadumal" ("planned, conceived") to "chto" ("what") so every word pulls its weight.
'It is not going to work.' Max holds a wry approach in the conversation, building the phrase around "poluchitsya" ("will come out") and "tebya" ("you") for a crisp, natural delivery.
Я скажу Саше, чтобы она тебе их вернула.
'I will tell Sasha to give them back to you.' Sasha conveys a clear style straight away, using "skazhu" (from "skazat", "I'll tell") alongside "vernula" ("returned, paid back") to shape the meaning.
'Max, you are amazing.' Sasha sustains a firm posture straight away, combining "super" ("super, great") and "maks" ("Max") so the key meaning lands right away.
'I do not have a boyfriend like that.' Sasha maintains a lively tempo across the room, using the everyday "u menya" ("by me") alongside "parnya" ("boyfriend") to show what belongs to the speaker.
'Well, I do.' Max shows a frank mood in their talk, putting "yest" ("there is") alongside "menya" ("me") in a tight, everyday turn of phrase.
'Did you want to say something to me?' Sasha asks sharply beside Max, putting "khotela" ("wanted, meant") alongside "skazat" ("tell") in a tight, everyday turn of phrase.
'I will pay you back for them tomorrow.' Max keeps a pointed style for Sasha, putting "zavtra" ("tomorrow") alongside "otdam" ("I give back") in a tight, everyday turn of phrase.
Я не понял, зачем тебе это надо?
Я скажу Саше, чтобы она тебе их вернула.

That wraps up this scene as max confronts Ilya about planting the earrings in Sasha's locker, and rather than admit the truth to Sasha, Max promises to pay Ilya for the jewelry tomorrow. Until next time!
